items.name: (a) Orlok part 14 motion-sensor typed but carries a live absolute-servo calibration window
evidence: data/character-3/parts.json part id "14": type="motion_sensor", modelId="pir_generic", pin 17 (current on-disk content, verified by direct read).

data/calibration_profiles.json key "3:14": {partId:14, capability:{kind:'absolute-servo',usMin:500,usMax:2500}, bounds:{minAngle:12,maxAngle:180}, autoGenerated:false, characterId:3, lastCalibratedAt:'2026-08-17T23:01:13.507Z'} — verified by direct read.

git log -p on data/character-3/parts.json shows part 14 was BRIEFLY retyped to a servo (modelId 'servo_miuzei_25kg') around 2026-02-22 and then reverted back to motion_sensor in the same window (diff visible in history). The calibration entry's lastCalibratedAt (2026-08-17) is ~6 months AFTER that revert, so someone hand-calibrated angle bounds for part 14 as a servo long after it was already a sensor again — this is current, live stale data, not a historical artifact.

data/calibration_profiles.json is gitignored ('data/calibration_profiles.json' in .gitignore, confirmed via git check-ignore -v; untracked since v8.1.4 per commit edba2196) — it is per-node runtime state, so this defect lives only on-disk on Orlok, not in git history.

Confirmed harmless today: routes/setup/calibration.js line 363-364 filters the calibration UI's positionable-parts list to types ['servo','linear_actuator','motor','stepper'] — motion_sensor is excluded, so the stray profile is not rendered as a servo control in /setup/calibration. It IS exposed raw via GET /setup/calibration/api/calibration/profiles (routes/setup/calibration.js:1483, 'Raw file dump: the scene/pose editors read presets off this') but part 14's presets array is empty, so no named position leaks through either. Currently dormant, not currently causing a visible bug, but it is wrong data sitting live on the Orlok node.
items.remaining_work: Data-only fix, no code change needed: delete (or reset to null/no-op) the '3:14' entry in /home/remote/MonsterBox/data/calibration_profiles.json on Orlok since part 14 is a PIR motion sensor and has no angle window. Confirm no other in-flight session is mid-calibrating part 14 before removing. Since the file is gitignored/per-node, this can't be fixed via a repo commit — it must be edited directly on the Orlok filesystem (and checked on any other node whose parts.json ever mislabeled a sensor as a servo, though I found no evidence of that on other characters).

items.name: (b) Sir Dragomir has no scenes/defaultSceneId and silently drops out of fleet queue loops
evidence: config/animatronics.json id:4 (Sir Dragomir) entry has 'defaultSceneId': null (direct read, current content).

services/orchestrationService.js:591-679 startAllQueueLoops(): for each controllable animatronic it reads animatronic.defaultSceneId; if falsy it returns {name, success:false, error:'No defaultSceneId configured'} for that node WITHOUT throwing — verified by reading the function body directly. The aggregate return is {success: successful>0, total, successful, results:[...]} (line 671-676), so Dragomir's failure item is present, named, with a specific reason, inside `results`.

routes/api/orchestrationRoutes.js:483 (POST /start-all-queue-loops) passes the service result straight through to res.json(result) with no filtering — the per-node failure is not swallowed in the API layer either.

views/orchestration/index.ejs has a logNodeFailures(r) function (comment: 'Per-node failures already travel in results[] and were being thrown away... Print them, named.') that iterates r.results.filter(x=>x.success===false) and writes a line '↳ Sir Dragomir: No defaultSceneId configured' to the visible command log every time Start Loops is triggered from the Fleet Command Center UI. git log -S"logNodeFailures" shows this landed in commit 9624a1c2 (v9.0.0) — well before the KNOWN-BUGS.md entry describing this as invisible was written.

docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md (added in commit 88c1c114, v10.0.1, dated 2026-08-19 01:14 -0500) currently says: 'Not an error the operator ever sees — the fleet call still reports overall success.' This is STALE relative to the code: the aggregate success:true framing is accurate (some nodes did succeed), but the claim that the operator never sees the per-node failure is refuted by the logNodeFailures UI code, which predates the doc entry by many versions.
items.remaining_work: The underlying data gap (Dragomir has zero scenes, no default scene) is real and still open — CONFIRMED, not refuted. Fix is data, not code: author at least one scene in data/character-4/scenes.json and set a defaultSceneId in config/animatronics.json id:4, OR make a deliberate operator decision that Dragomir intentionally has no queue-loop scene (a sentry/talker character who doesn't run an animation loop) and update docs to say so instead of calling it a bug. Separately: docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md's 'not an error the operator ever sees' clause should be corrected/removed since the FCC command log already surfaces it by name.

items.name: (c) PumpkinHead ElevenLabs agent prompt self-contradicts on audio tags
evidence: Live agent agent_0801k3f1dybkecj88sta18gwwrv5 fetched via mcp__claude_ai_ElevenLabs__agents_get (this session, MCP call succeeded despite the earlier system-reminder warning that ElevenLabs needs auth — it is in fact authorized here). Live prompt now reads consistently: '...You never use audio tags. Your voice is the tag.' in # Personality, and in # Tone: 'Do NOT use audio tags. Never write bracketed stage directions such as [laughs], [whispers], [shouts] or [sighs] — Pumpkinhead's delivery carries itself. Ellipses stretch the stalk… CAPITALS land the pounce. Those are the only two effects you use.' There is NO '# Audio Tags (expressive TTS)' section in the live prompt, and suggested_audio_tags is []. The live agent also gained two sections not in the checked-in snapshot ('# Interactivity', '# Names').

The checked-in snapshot at config/elevenlabs/agents/pumpkinhead.json (repo file, last touched by commit 92085963, 2026-08-16 04:14:55 -0500) STILL contains the old contradictory text: both 'You never use audio tags. Your voice is the tag.' AND a separate '# Audio Tags (expressive TTS)\nTwo per response maximum, placed right before the words they color: [laughs] [whispers] [shouts] [sighs]...' section that actively instructs using tags, while suggested_audio_tags is already [].

Live agent metadata.updated_at_unix_secs = 1787133342 = 2026-08-19 09:55:42 UTC. docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md's entry describing this contradiction as 'OPEN' was added in commit 88c1c114 at 2026-08-19 01:14:28 -0500 = 06:14:28 UTC, i.e. ~3h41m BEFORE the live agent's last update. So the live fix landed after the bug was logged, and the doc (and the repo snapshot) were never refreshed afterward.
items.remaining_work: No prompt fix needed — the live agent is already self-consistent. Two hygiene fixes remain: (1) refresh config/elevenlabs/agents/pumpkinhead.json to match the live agent verbatim (same pattern as commit 92085963's 'refresh agent snapshots to live' — fetch via agents_get and overwrite, matching metadata/version fields), and (2) remove or update the now-stale 'OPEN — PumpkinHead's agent prompt contradicts itself' line in docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md.

items.name: (d) text_normalisation_type inconsistent across the fleet (Orlok vs Mina/Dragomir)
evidence: Live fetch of all three agents this session confirms the inconsistency is real and current: Orlok (agent_0801k3f1dw7xe2g8r4jkbxk0gt2n) conversation_config.tts.text_normalisation_type = 'elevenlabs'; Mina (agent_8401k3f1dx98e05t94yp6kz4vf8n) = 'system_prompt'; Sir Dragomir (agent_7901k3f1dza1ee68w1257zh3s9x6) = 'system_prompt'.

Orlok's own prompt carries a 'Platform Configuration Notes' block (visible in the live prompt text) explaining a DIFFERENT, already-resolved issue: 'optimize_streaming_latency: 0 — set 2026-08-19. At 3 the platform applied max latency optimizations and disabled the text normalizer, which flattened the audio tags and the gravel into a smooth, fast, generic read.' This explanation is itself flagged as WRONG in docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md ('optimize_streaming_latency: 3 was mis-diagnosed as disabling the text normalizer. It does not; level 4 does... The real normalizer control is the separate text_normalisation_type field.') — so Orlok's in-prompt comment about why things are tuned the way they are is itself stale/incorrect, separate from the text_normalisation_type question.

docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md and docs/handoff/2026-08-19-v104-overnight.md:215 ('Mina's text_normalisation_type differs from Orlok's — reconcile or explain.') both confirm this was identified and explicitly left as an open, un-reconciled decision, not a solved item — no commit was found (via grep across docs/handoff and KNOWN-BUGS.md) reconciling it, and the live fetch this session confirms the split is still Orlok-alone vs the other two.

All three agents' overrides.conversation_config_override.tts fields (model_id, voice_id, stability, speed, similarity_boost, pronunciation_dictionary_locators) are hard-set to false in the live config, meaning nothing in MonsterBox's local tts-config.json can affect this at runtime regardless — text_normalisation_type must be changed at the agent level (ElevenLabs dashboard/API), not in the repo.
items.remaining_work: Aaron/operator decision needed, not a code fix: either (1) reconcile Orlok to 'system_prompt' like Mina and Dragomir for consistency, since Orlok's own prompt already carries explicit normalization instructions ('Numbers as words. Dates as words. No symbols spoken.' / 'Character Normalization: Numbers as words...') that would be redundant with the API-level 'elevenlabs' normalizer, or (2) document a real technical reason 'elevenlabs' server-side normalization is specifically needed for Orlok's heavy audio-tag/elongation style ([Romanian accent], stretched vowels like 'Cooome… clooser') that the other two don't use as intensively, and leave Mina/Dragomir on 'system_prompt'. Whichever is chosen, update docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md and docs/handoff/2026-08-19-v104-overnight.md to close the item instead of leaving it open with no rationale.

open_questions: Should the operator decide (d) now, or is it deliberately deferred to a future voice-tuning session? Recommend Aaron make the call since it trades off audio-tag fidelity vs. consistency, and no one has A/B tested Orlok on 'system_prompt' to see if it changes his delivery.

Item (a): was part 14 EVER a real servo hardware-wise, or was the brief 'servo_miuzei_25kg' relabeling in Feb 2026 itself a data-entry mistake (e.g. someone editing the wrong row)? If it was a genuine hardware swap-and-revert, worth checking whether any OTHER now-orphaned calibration_profiles.json entries exist for parts that changed type on any character (I only checked 3:14, the one named in the task).
dependencies_on_other_streams: None of the four items block or depend on other v11 streams' code changes — they are isolated data/config edits. Item (a) touches Orlok's local calibration_profiles.json which any concurrent calibration work on Orlok should be aware of (avoid clobbering an in-progress edit).
will_conflict_with: Any stream that also edits docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md this session (multiple items above recommend edits to the same file — Dragomir queue-loop entry and PumpkinHead audio-tags entry) should coordinate to avoid a merge fight on that single doc.
fleet_wide_notes: General pattern across all four items: MonsterBox's own docs (KNOWN-BUGS.md, docs/handoff/*) are themselves a stale layer on top of a stale layer — several 'OPEN' bugs I checked (Mina's ignore_default_personality, Mina's suggested_audio_tags, PumpkinHead's audio-tag contradiction, the FCC 'silent success' framing) turned out to already be FIXED live or in code, just not reflected in the docs. Treat every KNOWN-BUGS.md/handoff claim as a hypothesis to re-verify against the live agent or the current file, never as ground truth — this matches the repo's own stated recurring defect.
